subtopic: Facing an ethical breach at work
passage:
I still wince when I think about that Monday review. I'm Tushar. A report from Trisha's team looked wrong to me, and I had been angry about it all weekend. So when Trisha finished presenting, I said in front of everyone, "These numbers can't be right. Somebody is fudging them."
I had no proof. I hadn't asked Trisha a single question beforehand.
Trisha's face closed. "Show me," Trisha said. I couldn't. The room went quiet, and the meeting moved on with people avoiding my eyes.
The real problem, a mismatch between two reports, sat there for weeks because Trisha would barely speak to me. I had wanted it fixed, and I had made sure it wouldn't be.

qa.q: What did Tushar say in front of everyone?
qa.a: Tushar said, "These numbers can't be right. Somebody is fudging them."

qa.q: What was Tushar feeling before the meeting?
qa.a: Tushar was angry, having been furious about the report all weekend.

qa.q: What could Tushar have done before the meeting instead?
qa.a: Tushar could have asked Trisha privately to walk through the numbers and brought the actual mismatch on paper.

qa.q: How might Trisha have felt being called out in front of everyone?
qa.a: Trisha probably felt embarrassed and defensive, which shows in the closed face and the challenge to show the proof.

grounding: The reflection shows an employee angry at a senior colleague who raises a concern in a group meeting without evidence or a private talk, making the colleague defensive.

subtopic: Facing an ethical breach at work
passage:
Coaching note, Thursday.
In today's project review, Sahil interrupted Eshaan's update in front of eleven people: 'You're hiding the delay from the client, and everyone knows it.' He had no slide, no dates, nothing on paper. Eshaan went red, said the delay had been agreed with the client last week, and the next forty minutes became an argument about tone instead of the schedule. Two people left early. Afterwards Eshaan asked me whether Sahil was 'out to get' him.
The concern may still be real; I don't know yet. But the way it was raised made it harder to examine. I met Sahil at five. He was shaken and a bit defiant. We agreed he would write down what he saw with dates and talk to Eshaan privately first, with me present if he wanted.
Mentor, delivery team

qa.q: How many people were in the room when Sahil interrupted?
How was Sahil feeling when the mentor met him at five?
qa.a: He was shaken and a bit defiant, probably still sure of his concern but aware the meeting had gone badly.

qa.q: What other approach would have made Sahil's concern easier to examine?
qa.a: Writing down what he saw with dates and raising it privately with Eshaan or a manager first, so the facts could be checked without an audience.

qa.q: How did the meeting feel for Eshaan?
qa.a: Eshaan felt attacked in front of the team, went red and even wondered whether Sahil was out to get him.

grounding: It shows a mentor's note on an employee who calls out a senior colleague in a meeting without evidence, making the colleague defensive and burying the real concern.

subtopic: Facing an ethical breach at work
passage:
Monday night.
I did the stupid thing. In the 10 a.m. team call, with the regional head listening, I said, 'Nitin, your vendor quotes are padded and you know it.' I'd seen two quotes that looked high. That's all I had. No figures on my screen, no talk with him first.
Nitin didn't shout. He just went very still and said, 'Send me what you're referring to.' I couldn't. The regional head ended the call early.
By lunch, Nitin had written to the head that he felt publicly accused. By evening, my own manager was asking why I hadn't come to her first. And now nobody's looking at the quotes. They're looking at me.
If the quotes really are padded, I've made it harder to prove.
Tarun

qa.q: What did Nitin say after going still?
What is Tarun feeling on Monday night?
qa.a: Tarun feels embarrassed and regretful, aware that the outburst moved attention from the quotes to Tarun.

qa.q: What would you change first if you were Tarun?
qa.a: Gather the two quotes and compare them with market prices, then raise it privately with the manager before any meeting.

qa.q: What was the call like for Nitin?
qa.a: Nitin felt publicly accused in front of the regional head, which made him guarded and pushed him to complain.

grounding: It shows an employee accusing a senior colleague in a team call without evidence or prior talk, making him defensive and undermining the concern.
